body:
As far as the implementation goes, it looks like a clean copy with no loss of functionality (except ordering, which is a good thing). 
<sub> Edit: should have looked much closer :/ </sub>
Some minor things to potentially consider but overall looks good to me. 

I am surprised by the reported loss of performance (haven't checked on my machine, so I can't confirm nor deny, and will trust DeeJay). But the only additional costs I can see are a few cases where you get an extra pointer indirection, but that shouldn't be very expensive. Remarkably, I would actually expect it to get faster thanks to eliminating some for loops in favor of `GDType`'s self & combined maps.

Turns out the CI error wasn't unrelated, unlike I assumed for my earlier positive review.

In rewriting `ClassDB::get_method_list()` and `ClassDB::get_method_list_with_compatibility()` to use the new `gdtype->get_method_map()` you got rid of the virtual methods from the "return" `List<MethodInfo> *p_methods`. 

Highlighted the two erroneous removals in comments and potential fixes.
Otherwise, a `ClassDB::get_virtual_methods_with_compatibility()` must be added and every caller site of both methods must have the associated virtual method added.

The two checks for `type->disabled` will not behave in this PR the same way as they used to due to using `gdtype->get_method_map(p_no_inheritance)` instead of the old looping through every single type. 

Assuming `p_no_inheritance == false`, otherwise it's not relevant
Before: type -> check disabled -> add methods if not -> supertype replaces type -> loop
After: type -> check disabled -> add all methods of self and all supertypes

This means we go from only including methods for type and all non-disabled supertypes to including methods for type and all supertypes if type is not disabled. 

This can be handled:
A. By reintroducing the loops and using `gdtype->get_method_map(true)`
B. By changing the way method maps are handled on `GDType` to take into account disabled types when using `get_method_map(false)`

LGTM!

The type disabling issues should be adressed in a follow-up PR, but are safe to leave as-is since the disabling behavior is seemingly never used (possibly dead code). 
Could be worth moving the `if (type->disabled)` checks outside of the loop to avoid an unnecessary lookup and the iterations which will all fail if disabled, but that's not a blocker in any way.

Although my stress tests still report a performance loss, I'm hopeful an eventual move of property maps into `GDType` will be the definitive performance improvement that will cover it (it's the only thing keeping `ClassDB::get_property()` from not doing super-type looping).

Can't pretend I'm fully versed in this part of the engine (especially in 4.x) but from a look through, the aims of moving to `GDType` seem worthwhile.

This PR:
* Fixes the stability bug after hot-reload with the soft leaks
* Gets rid of the method order difference in debug and release

Things to note:
* there does seem a performance regression with `AHashMap` - this isn't a blocker imo. This temporary regression will become a net positive once more is moved out of `ClassDB`
* I'm assuming the soft leaks have been checked they don't produce too much memory bloat
* documentation may be affected (where methods were previously badly classified)
